data.title: The Fed Will Have to Raise Interest Rates More, Even If It Pauses in October — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Nicole Goodkind

Federal Reserve officials appear inclined to keep interest rates unchanged at their Oct. 27-28 policy meeting. But don't be fooled by a pause: More rate increases are likely coming, possibly as soon as December, to tame escalating inflation.

The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September, to a target range of 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023. Officials have since indicated that they want more time to assess the economy before making another move.

There is plenty to assess, and some of it isn't encouraging.

The consumer price index rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier. That was a stronger-than-expected increase and a sizable jump up from August's 3.4% annual growth rate. Prices climbed o.6% month to month in September, with a 9.1% jump in gasoline accounting for more than half the increase. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, accelerated to 2.6% annually from 2.4% in August.

There were signs of broader price pressures, too. Airfares, education, recreation, and used vehicles all became more expensive.

Producer prices surged 1.3% in September, their largest monthly gain in four years. Wholesale prices were up 6.3% from a year earlier, raising concerns that businesses could pass additional costs on to consumers in the coming months.

The numbers strengthened the case for higher interest rates, but markets don't think the latest data changed the Fed's apparent preference for waiting until later this year to raise rates. The latest reports make a December increase more likely, said James McCann at Edward Jones. He expects one increase in 2027, as well.

"The Fed won't panic in the face of these numbers, but the data will add to the conviction on the FOMC [Federal Open Market Committee] that policy needs to be tighter to help drag inflation back to target," he wrote in a note Friday.

Inflation has run above the Fed's 2% annual target for more than five years. Central bank officials spent the week explaining why they are concerned about inflation without committing to an immediate rise in rates.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called Wednesday's CPI report discouraging. But in an interview with Yahoo Finance, he cautioned against placing too much weight on a single report.

"I don't think we yet know the answer to that," he said when asked if more rate hikes are needed. But "if we get more months like this...that's totally unacceptable," he said of the inflation report.

Speaking in Bangkok on Wednesday, Fed governor Michelle Bowman said she saw no urgency to adjust rates again. "We have some time to wait and see how financial conditions evolve before we take more action," she said.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly suggested that further tightening would probably be needed but not at the next meeting. "Why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency?" Daly said Wednesday in an interview with Reuters. "We have more meetings ahead of us."

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack offered an argument for acting sooner, however. In remarks Monday, she warned that inflation is becoming increasingly broad-based and that businesses are beginning to incorporate higher costs into their pricing plans. "When feasible, I generally think it's preferable to make smaller adjustments, and to do so relatively quickly, rather than to wait and risk needing a larger course correction," Hammack said at the meeting of the National Association for Business Economics (NABE) in Cleveland, Ohio.

On Thursday, speaking at an event held by Goldman Sachs, she warned that deteriorating inflation expectations could require more aggressive rate increases. The warning caused some to speculate that a half-percentage-point increase is on the table later this year.

The Fed's Beige Book, released Wednesday, showed economic growth slowing in parts of the country, with hiring subdued and lower-income consumers pulling back on spending. Businesses reported rising costs from energy and tariffs, and noted that customers were becoming less able to absorb higher prices.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered little indication Thursday evening that the latest data had changed his thinking. Speaking in Bangkok, he said economic developments since the September meeting had matched the Fed's expectations.

"I don't prejudge meetings," Warsh said.

Investors took his comments as another reason to expect a pause. They are now pricing in an 83% chance that rates remain unchanged at the October meeting, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Expectations for an increase had briefly surged following Wednesday's inflation report.

The Fed's October meeting will take place less than a week before the midterm elections.

Research by CME Group's Mark Shore found that the Fed left interest rates unchanged between Oct. 1 and Election Day in about two-thirds of election years from 1972 through 2024.

This past week's data and Fed speakers suggest more monetary tightening might be merited later in the year, but the September increase may have bought the Fed some time.

For now, investors and economists are looking past October to a possible December increase.

Write to Nicole Goodkind at nicole.goodkind@barrons.com

data.title: Renault Duster Strong Hybrid takes on Toyota, Maruti Suzuki with ₹16.99 lakh price, 29 km/l mileage
data.description:
Renault’s Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160 enters India’s strong-hybrid passenger-vehicle market, estimated at 1.23 lakh units in FY26, with a starting price of ₹16.99 lakh and claimed mileage of 29 km/l. The French automaker is targeting diesel SUV buyers as it challenges Toyota and Maruti Suzuki.

With Renault’s retail market share below 1 per cent, the Duster must convert its fuel-efficiency advantage into sustained sales against established Toyota and Maruti Suzuki hybrids and diesel SUVs backed by stronger dealership networks and customer loyalty.

The Duster is priced ₹31,000 above the entry-level Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara Strong Hybrid at ₹16.68 lakh and broadly in line with Toyota’s Urban Cruiser Hyryder Strong Hybrid, priced from around ₹16.81 to 17.18 lakh. However, its 1.8-litre petrol engine and dual-motor system deliver 160 PS, against 116 PS from the 1.5-litre hybrid systems in both rivals. Renault also claims better mileage than their 27.97 km/l, while its 1.4-kWh battery enables electric-only operation for up to 80 per cent of city driving time, depending on conditions.

Speaking to reporters after the launch, Renault Group India Chief Executive Officer Stéphane Deblaise said the hybrid would expand the Duster’s customer base beyond its petrol variants, allowing it to compete more directly for diesel SUV buyers.

Strong-hybrid registrations rose 9.5 per cent to 86,403 units during January–September 2026, from 78,881 a year earlier, according to previously compiled vehicle-registration data. Despite the growth, the category remains a small part of India’s passenger-vehicle market.

Diesel alternative

During the media roundtable, Deblaise positioned strong hybrids as an alternative to diesel vehicles, citing fuel efficiency, lower total cost of ownership and driving refinement. He said consumers could not move overnight from internal-combustion vehicles to battery-electric cars.

Renault said it has sold more than one million vehicles equipped with its hybrid technology globally, providing an established technology base for its India introduction.

Product offensive

The launch is part of Renault’s seven-model roadmap through 2030, spanning petrol, CNG, strong-hybrid and electric vehicles across two platforms. The company is preparing the sub-four-metre Bridger SUV for late 2027, followed by an electric model expected in 2028.

Management, however, clarified that there are no immediate plans to introduce the Duster’s hybrid system in smaller models such as the Kwid, Triber and Kiger. Adapting the technology would require significant engineering and packaging changes, Deblaise said.

Renault is also expanding its CNG offerings and targeting up to 90 per cent localisation across future product programmes to improve cost competitiveness. It has outlined an ambition of €2 billion in annual exports by 2030, covering vehicles, components and engineering services.

Ownership challenge

Beyond pricing and efficiency, Renault must address concerns over hybrid maintenance, battery reliability, spare-parts costs and service accessibility.

During the post-launch interaction, Deblaise acknowledged gaps in service infrastructure and parts pricing, saying Renault was examining additional localisation opportunities while strengthening existing facilities and dealer training.

With Renault’s retail market share below 1 per cent, the Duster must convert its fuel-efficiency advantage into sustained sales against established Toyota and Maruti Suzuki hybrids and diesel SUVs backed by stronger dealership networks and customer loyalty.

data.title: Jindal Ferrous Enters Carbon Steel Market With Rs 5,000 Cr Odisha Plant
data.description:
The 2.2 million tonne facility brings integrated steelmaking, automation and waste recycling under one roof as the company expands its presence in the domestic carbon steel market

Jindal Ferrous has entered integrated carbon steel manufacturing with a Rs 5,000 crore investment in Jajpur, Odisha. The new facility, inaugurated by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on 14 October 2026, can produce 2.2 million tonnes of steel annually.

The plant gives the company a production base to serve customers across India, particularly in the northern and eastern regions, where infrastructure projects and industrial activity support demand for carbon steel. Its immediate priority is to ramp up operations and establish a customer base.

Integrated Steelmaking Operations

The Jajpur facility combines a sinter plant, blast furnace, steel melting shop, and supporting infrastructure. By housing these operations at one location, Jindal Ferrous can manage several stages of steel production within the same complex.

Resource recovery also forms part of the plant’s operating design. The facility processes metallurgical waste through its sinter plant and reuses process gases, measures intended to improve material utilisation and limit waste generation.

The blast furnace incorporates a Level-2 automation platform, an expert model, high top-pressure operation and dry gas-cleaning systems. These technologies are designed to support process control, production stability and operating efficiency.

International Technology Support

The company has partnered with Japan’s JFE Steel Corporation for technical support during the plant’s operational ramp-up and steel production.

Several international suppliers have contributed equipment and technology. Germany’s SMS Group, through Paul Wurth, supplied the blast furnace technology. Sweden’s UHT provided the Granshot system, while Austria’s Primetals Technologies supplied technology for the sinter plant, basic oxygen furnace shop and caster. Italy’s Danieli provided equipment for the ladle furnace and hot-metal desulphurisation system.

These partnerships support the company’s effort to establish integrated steelmaking operations and achieve reliable production as the facility moves towards its intended operating levels.

Building A Steel Cluster

The investment adds another manufacturing facility to the Jindal group’s presence in Jajpur. Jindal Stainless has increased its production capacity at the site from 0.8 million tonnes to 2.2 million tonnes over the past two decades, according to the company.

The group is also pursuing plans to expand the industrial ecosystem around its operations. Jindal Stainless has laid the foundation for a proposed stainless steel park covering more than 270 acres. The park is designed to host over 180 downstream and ancillary units, with the potential to create more than 15,000 jobs.

A Centre of Excellence is also planned to develop skills, support technology adoption and strengthen downstream manufacturing. The proposed park could create business opportunities for suppliers, logistics operators, maintenance providers and other ancillary businesses as the industrial cluster develops. The extent of these opportunities will depend on the establishment of downstream units and supporting services.

data.title: Jailed Mahadev Scam Accused Secretly Mortgages US Headquarters Despite ED Freeze
data.description:
Eraaya Hides $12.6M US Mortgage From Stock Markets As Mahadev Scam Net Tightens Around Ebix. The $12.6 million loan was taken after chairman Vikas Garg's arrest, despite a written order from the Enforcement Directorate not to create any lien.

Mahadev betting syndicate has a sensational new story of a stunning international asset maneuver.

While Vikas Garg—the high-flying chairman of Ebix Inc. and Eraaya Lifespaces—sits in the custody of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in Raipur, his corporate empire has secretly pawned off its crown jewel.

The company's massive 17-acre corporate headquarters in Johns Creek, Atlanta, has been leveraged for a staggering $12.6 million loan.

India's ED says Ebix, a Nasdaq listed company, was purchased using the Mahadev betting money and those involved ran a corporate empire through hawala channels.

Eraya Lifescience is an Indian listed company associated with Garg and ED has frozen all its assets.

The recent cross-border twist directly flouts an explicit, high-priority Provisional Attachment Order (No. 16/2026) issued by the ED on June 5, 2026. That order locked down Rs 940.77 crore in assets, specifically targeting Eraaya’s shareholding in Ebix.

Authorities flatly state the company was acquired entirely using laundered gambling cash generated by the notorious SkyExchange ecosystem and processed via Dubai hawala networks.

____________________

The Midnight Deal in Georgia

Despite a written, legal command from Indian agencies warning Ebix leadership "not to allow any sale, transfer, alienation, or modification of lien," corporate operatives in the United States moved under the cover of darkness.On August 4, 2026—exactly three weeks after Garg was dramatically arrested at his Delhi residence—Ebix’s US President Gagan Sethi signed a legally binding "Deed to Secure Debt" with California-based lender Velocity Commercial Capital LLC.Recorded under Deed Book 70417 in Georgia land records on August 12, the explosive documents reveal that Ebix "irrevocably and unconditionally" mortgaged the iconic 1 Ebix Way campus.

Worse still, Ebix brazenly assured the American lender that it held the full "right to encumber the Property," completely erasing any mention of the active, multi-million-dollar criminal freeze slapped on it by India.

______________________

Siphoning Assets Before Confiscation

The $12.6 million note, which locks the property down until 2056, also signs over all of the building's rental income to the California lender. Sources close to the development reveal that $11.5 million of the fresh cash was immediately burned to pay off a pre-existing lien held by deep-pocketed investors Watch Hill and Melanie Lane, who had invested in both Ebix and Eraaya.What makes this maneuver deeply alarming to Indian investigators is the timing and intent.

By borrowing heavily against the Atlanta campus, the corporate entity is effectively stripping the physical asset of its value. Every dollar bled out of the US headquarters means one less dollar for the Indian government to recover if the courts order a final asset confiscation.Adding fuel to the fire, the property is already being aggressively flipped. The campus has been quietly listed for sale via broker Cresa, with healthcare giant Emory Healthcare—whose Johns Creek hospital sits right next door—reportedly waiting in the wings to buy the property outright.

___________________

The Great Corporate Cover-Up & Bail in Jeopardy

While American property deeds expose the transaction in broad daylight, Eraaya Lifespaces has maintained a total radio silence on the Indian stock exchanges. The company has actively hidden the $12.6 million mortgage from Indian regulators and public shareholders, completely failing to make mandatory disclosures.This hidden debt bomb contains a lethal trap: the US mortgage states that any "attachment or similar process" by authorities constitutes an immediate event of default.

If the ED attempts to globally enforce its seizure of the Atlanta campus, Velocity Commercial Capital is legally entitled to call in the loan, potentially triggering chaotic international legal warfare over the property.The revelation of this rogue financial maneuver is expected to trigger an absolute firestorm in the Indian courts.

Garg, the former convener of the Delhi BJP’s Economic Cell, is currently fighting for his freedom. However, bail guidelines strictly require judges to weigh whether an accused person can manipulate evidence or liquidate dirty assets.

With proof that his corporate entities are actively draining value from frozen properties while he is behind bars, Garg's chances of securing bail have likely gone up in flames.

Because an Indian ED order cannot directly block a Georgia land registry, New Delhi must now frantically activate Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties (MLAT) to halt the transaction before the Mahadev betting loot vanishes into the American financial system forever.

____________________________

The London Conspiracy & The Master Architect

Behind the clinical terminology of this corporate takeover lay a series of clandestine, high-stakes meetings in London. It was here that Delhi businessman Vikas Garg sat across from Hari Shankar Tibrewal, a notorious, Dubai-based hawala kingpin alleged to be a primary pillar of the Mahadev Online Book empire.Tibrewal wasn’t just moving money; he was the ultimate financial architect.

While ED records show row after row of the words "Not Appeared" next to his name following repeated summons, investigators have firmly placed the Kolkata-born operator at the center of the money's journey from betting app to boardroom.In their London strategy sessions, Garg and Tibrewal sketched out a wildly ambitious plan: use the hyper-lucrative, illegal cash flow generated by the SkyExchange betting platform to cross oceans and swallow a prestigious, Nasdaq-listed American tech giant.

____________________________

The SkyExchange Mirage and the Hawala Pipeline

SkyExchange operated as a massive digital hoover, sucking in crores of rupees daily from thousands of punters across states like Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh. The scale of the operation was staggering. The ED's prosecution complaints describe the platform as co-owned and co-promoted by Tibrewal alongside scam kingpins Sourabh Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal.

* SkyExchange Production: Generated ₹22 crore a week across 178 documented weeks—accounting for rs 3,916 crore in crime proceeds from that platform alone.

* Lotus365 Synergy: Run by Girish Talreja, this allied arm added another Rs 50 crore a month.

Taken together, this shadow ecosystem was producing an off-the-books turnover of Rs 4,000–5,000 crore a year—matching the output of a legitimate mid-cap company.Through a dizzying web of shell companies, mirror accounts, and untraceable ledgers managed out of Dubai, Tibrewal successfully transformed this dirty cash into clean corporate capital.

The money was routed back into India via sophisticated financial instruments—including Qualified Institutional Placements (QIPs), Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPIs), and Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs)—pumped directly into listed entities controlled by Garg.

________________________________

From Rs 13 Penny Stock to a $361 Million Global Empire

The most spectacular illusion in this financial thriller was the meteoric, logic-defying rise of Justride Enterprises, a virtually unknown penny stock trading at a measly Rs 13. Rebranded as Eraaya Lifespaces, the company suddenly exploded by an astronomical 6,000% in a single year, hitting nearly Rs 800 per share by August 2024 as it became the primary vehicle for the laundered funds.

Weaponising this manufactured financial muscle, Eraaya stunned the corporate world by walking into a US bankruptcy court and winning a $361 million auction for Ebix Inc., a collapsed insurance-software pioneer. It was the ultimate corporate camouflage: an American tech giant bought out using the pocket money of millions of unsuspecting online bettors, completing a dirty cash pipeline stretching from the alleys of Raipur to the glass boardrooms of Atlanta.

_____________________________

Palak Shah

BW Reporters

Palak Shah is a seasoned investigative journalist and the fearless author of The Market Mafia: Chronicle of India’s High-Tech Stock Market Scandal & The Cabal That Went Scot-Free, a hard-hitting exposé that unmasked the shadowy underbelly of India’s financial markets. With nearly two decades of boots-on-the-ground reporting in Mumbai, Palak has carved a reputation as a relentless truth-seeker, diving deep into the nexus of money, power, and regulation. His bylines have graced India’s most prestigious financial dailies, including The Economic Times, Business Standard, The Financial Express, and The Hindu Business Line, where his incisive coverage has shaped narratives and rattled boardrooms.

Drawn to crime reporting at the tender age of 19, Palak quickly realized that Mumbai’s gritty gang wars of the 1980s had given way to a slicker, more insidious form of organized crime—white-collar schemes orchestrated in corporate towers. This epiphany fueled his pivot to financial journalism, where he’s spent years decoding the complex machinations of India’s ‘white money’ economy.

From stock market manipulations to regulatory loopholes, Palak’s work peels back the polished veneer of high finance to reveal the cabals pulling the strings. His passion for uncovering truth, backed by a knack for connecting dots others miss, makes him a formidable voice in Indian journalism, unafraid to challenge the status quo and expose the players who think they’re untouchable.

data.title: India's ICICI Bank Q2 profit rises 20.1%, beats estimates
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

Indian private lender ICICI Bank reported a higher-than-expected profit for its second quarter on Saturday, driven by stronger loan demand and lower provisions for bad loans.

The country's second-largest private lender by market capitalisation posted a standalone net profit of 148.43 billion Indian rupees ($1.56 billion) for the three months ended September, compared with 123.59 billion rupees a year earlier.

Analysts had expected a profit of 142.51 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Indian lenders have seen strong loan growth during the quarter across both corporate and retail segments.

ICICI Bank's net interest income rose 17.7% to 253.39 billion rupees, aided by a 30% increase in total loans. Deposits grew 27.1% from a year earlier.

Its net interest margin, a key measure of profitability, narrowed to 4.18% from 4.36% in the previous quarter.

Funds kept aside for potential bad loans and other losses fell 6.9% to 8.51 billion rupees.

The bank's other income, which includes income from bonds and other investments, rose 6.2% to 80.47 billion rupees amid volatile currency and debt markets.

The lender's asset quality improved, with the gross non-performing asset ratio at 1.20% at the end of September, compared with 1.38% in the prior three months.

($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

data.title: Indian state food safety authority names Blinkit, Reliance executives in expired food probe
data.description:
By Arpan Chaturvedi

India's food safety authority has named officials of Reliance Group entities and of Eternal’s Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.

The Food and Drug Administration of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai’s most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino’s and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald’s outlet.

The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world’s most populous country.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.

"The disposal agencies ... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.

In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.

Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

"Any attempt to divert expired, damaged or consumer-rejected food products meant for destruction back into the market is a serious matter that demands strict scrutiny and accountability," Maharashtra's FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters.

"No company, brand, business or individual is above the law when it comes to food safety."

INDIA'S INTENSIFYING CRACKDOWN

Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s business group. Zomato’s Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.

The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.

"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."

The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state — three Reliance and two Eternal entities, the case documents said.

Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.

In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo , Nestle , Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.

data.title: Judge Rejects Gemini And CFTC Bid To Overturn $5 Million Settlement
data.description:
TL;DR: A federal judge has rejected a joint attempt by Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to overturn the exchange’s $5 million settlement. The decision leaves the existing judgment in place despite the regulator’s changed approach to cryptocurrency enforcement.

Gemini has failed in an unusual attempt to undo a regulatory settlement, despite having the very agency that brought the original case on its side.

US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected a joint motion by the exchange and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission seeking to vacate a consent judgment entered in January 2025.

The settlement arose from allegations that Gemini misled the regulator during its review of a proposed Bitcoin futures product in 2017. Gemini agreed to pay a $5 million penalty and accepted a permanent injunction.

When Regulators Change Their Minds

The CFTC subsequently reconsidered the original enforcement case as its digital asset priorities evolved. Together with Gemini, it asked the court to revisit the settlement.

That is a very different situation from the more familiar legal battle in which an exchange disputes a regulator’s allegations. This time, both parties wanted relief from the court’s earlier judgment.

But a change in enforcement policy does not automatically erase a final court order. The judge found that the arguments presented did not satisfy the legal standards for reopening the settlement.

The decision is significant for other cryptocurrency businesses hoping that a more accommodating federal regulatory environment might undo historical enforcement outcomes.

What Changes For Gemini?

In the immediate term, very little. The settlement remains in effect and the court has not imposed a new fine.

The wider message is more important: courts retain control of their judgments, even when a regulatory agency changes its view of a case.

Washington’s approach to cryptocurrency may have become more favourable, but companies cannot assume that previously approved settlements will disappear alongside the political circumstances in which they were reached.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: ICICI Bank Q2 results: Net profit rises 20% to Rs 14,843 crore, beats estimates; NII up 18%
data.description:
ICICI Bank on Saturday reported a 20.1 percent year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 14,843 crore for the second quarter of FY27, beating market expectations. The private sector lender also reported stronger-than-expected growth in net interest income (NII).

The bank's net profit exceeded the CNBC TV18 poll estimate of Rs 14,280 crore, which had projected a 16 percent year-on-year increase. The reported profit was approximately 3.9 percent higher than the estimate.

Net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 17.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 25,338.7 crore, compared with the poll estimate of Rs 24,811 crore. The reported NII was approximately 2.1 percent above expectations.

The results indicated stronger-than-anticipated growth in both profitability and core interest income during the July-September quarter.

ICICI Bank share price

ICICI Bank shares closed 0.55 percent higher at Rs 1,397 on Friday, ahead of the quarterly earnings announcement. The stock has gained 4.4 percent so far in 2026, outperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined 11.5 percent during the same period. data.title: Dan Ives Calls CoreWeave Sell-Off A ‘False Narrative’ — Sees Buying Opportunity With AI Demand Accelerating As CRWV Stock Sees Worst Week In 11 Months
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives said he views the recent pressure on CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure stocks as a buying opportunity, pointing to the company's demand and backlog as reasons to look beyond the near-term volatility.
  • He added that he sees a major disconnect between the market's concerns and the underlying demand picture.
  • Ives said his recent trip to South Korea reinforced his conviction that demand across the AI hardware ecosystem continues to accelerate, particularly in memory.

CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV) shares are facing their worst week in nearly a year as investor concerns over the AI infrastructure company's debt load and rising borrowing costs intensify.

But Yorkville Ives Partner and Senior Managing Director analyst Dan Ives sees the recent sell-off as an overreaction. Ives argued during an interview with Bloomberg on Friday that the broader AI demand story remains intact even as investors reassess the economics of debt-heavy data center companies.

CoreWeave shares closed nearly 12% lower on Friday, falling about 1% further during the afterhours session. CoreWeave shares are now down over 25% this week, which is the worst weekly decline since a roughly 26% fall in November 2025.

CoreWeave Sell-Off Is A ‘False Narrative,’ Says Ives

Ives said he views the recent pressure on CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure stocks as a buying opportunity, pointing to the company's demand and backlog as reasons to look beyond the near-term volatility, while adding that he sees a major disconnect between the market's concerns and the underlying demand picture.

“When you think about what's happening in CoreWeave, given the worries in terms of the debt and what's happened with CDS spreads, I view it as similar to ‘SaaS apocalypse’ earlier this year,” he said.

While Ives acknowledged that higher interest rates could create challenges, he argued that the strength of AI demand ultimately outweighs those concerns.

“I'm not saying there's not some issues in terms as rates go higher. But given the demand, given backlog, I think this is ultimately a false narrative,” he said, while noting that the sharp decline in AI-related stocks has created an opportunity for investors.

AI Demand Is Accelerating, Ives Says

Ives said his recent trip to South Korea reinforced his conviction that demand across the AI hardware ecosystem continues to accelerate, particularly in memory.

“Memory, if I look at chips, we've seen demand accelerate 30%, 40% over the last 60 and 90 days,” he said.

For Ives, that acceleration is an important signal for the broader AI trade. He expects upcoming earnings from hyperscalers and other technology companies to provide another test of whether the massive spending cycle is continuing.

“So what that speed boost is showing is that this is all accelerating in terms as it plays out. That to me, continues to be the best barometer for what we're seeing,” he said.

He argued that investors should focus less on near-term volatility and more on whether demand for AI infrastructure continues to build.

“And I think we're going to see that in earnings relative to the hyperscalers, relative to broader tech. Focus on demand and demand is telling you we are in the third inning relative to this AI game,” he added.

Ives also acknowledged that political opposition could prevent some data center projects from moving forward, estimating that 5% to 10% could ultimately be rejected or delayed. But he said that would not fundamentally derail the AI infrastructure buildout.

Even with that potential pushback, he argued that the scale of the remaining opportunity is enormous, with data center spending continuing to have a broad impact across the technology sector.

“But still to that point, you're going to have 800 to 1,000 data centers out there,” Ives said, adding that capital spending could have a “6 to 7x multiplier” relative to the rest of tech, which he said remains central to his core AI thesis.

Jefferies Says CoreWeave Sell-Off Is Overdone

According to TheFly, Jefferies is also pushing back against the recent pressure on CoreWeave, with analyst Brent Thill maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating and a $150 price target on the stock.

Thill said the market's reaction to rising yields on CoreWeave's unsecured debt has been too harsh and does not reflect the company's underlying fundamentals.

“While future funding costs could rise, short-duration deals at about $40 million per MW more than offset this,” the firm said in a research note.

Jefferies consequently views the recent decline in CoreWeave shares as excessive.

What Retail Investors Think About CRWV Stock

data.title: Your Insurer Is Cutting Your Medicare Advantage Plan. Here's What to Do. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Janna Herron

Insurers that offer Medicare Advantage (MA) healthcare plans have been scaling back plans or eliminating them altogether, leaving millions of retirees in the lurch.

Indeed, many of the people who pick a Medicare Advantage plan during open enrollment that runs from Oct. 15 to Dec. 7 may only be in that plan for a year or two before it, too, goes away.

If you are one of the more than 35 million seniors enrolled in Medicare Advantage, here's what you need to know if your coverage suddenly changes or disappears.

How is Medicare Advantage different?

Unlike traditional Medicare, which is accepted by almost all doctors and hospitals, Medicare Advantage operates much like employer-provided insurance. You pay lower costs if you stay within a network of doctors and providers, and pay higher out-of-network charges if you seek care elsewhere.

The lure for many Medicare Advantage plans is you pay no monthly premium, though you still must pay your monthly Medicare premium to the Social Security Administration. By contrast, if you use traditional Medicare and supplemental, or Medigap, insurance, you will pay a private insurance premium in addition to your Medicare premium.

Medicare Advantage can save you money if you stay well. But if you get sick, you often have to pay substantial deductibles and copays, which can make MA more expensive than traditional Medicare plus supplemental insurance. You also may need to get prior authorizations from your insurer before beginning a new treatment or undergoing a recommended procedure.

Why are plan terminations happening?

In 2026, 2.6 million seniors saw their Medicare Advantage plans terminated, representing 13% of enrollees in MA plans with drug coverage, according to a KFF analysis. That was more than double the percentage from the year before. The percentage excludes seniors enrolled in MA special needs plans, plans without prescription drug coverage and those with employer coverage.

This year has seen similar moves from larger insurers like Humana, UnitedHealthcare and Molina Healthcare along with smaller plan providers such as Clear Spring Health and Presbyterian Health.

Insurers say costs for offering these plans continue to increase. Seniors are seeking healthcare services at higher rates and certain drug prices keep rising.

At the same time, federal payments for offering these plans are increasing at a slower pace, squeezing insurers' profit margins. And now, due to a federal rule change, insurers are footing a larger portion of prescription drug costs after enrollees exceed their out-of-pocket spending limit.

"Insurance companies are now deciding, 'We don't want to just lose our shirts all day long. Let's take our ball and go home,'" said Melinda Caughill, co-founder of 65 Incorporated, which provides Medicare consulting services.

What can MA seniors do?

If your insurer is getting rid of your plan, it must send you a notice. Right now — with Medicare open enrollment season heating up — it may be easy to miss it.

"People are going to be absolutely inundated with advertisements [and] mailings to try to persuade people to enroll in plans," said David Lipschutz, co-director of law and policy for the Center for Medicare Advocacy. "So sometimes the official notifications from someone's actual plan can get lost in the shuffle."

If you do nothing after getting the notice, you will be enrolled in a replacement plan. But you can also select a new Medicare Advantage plan that fits you best. The key is to make sure your preferred physicians and provider networks along with your prescription medicines are covered by any new MA plan you sign up for.

Another option is switching to traditional Medicare. That has its own issues, such as pricey or even denied Medigap plans, the supplemental policies that cover the 20% of medical costs that traditional Medicare doesn't pay.

If your current MA plan is ceasing altogether or your insurer is pulling out of your area, you should get a right to purchase a Medigap plan without undergoing any underwriting, according to Lipschutz. That means you can't get denied or charged more because of a health condition.

But if your MA plan is merging into another plan in the same area by the same insurer, that doesn't necessarily trigger the right to purchase a Medigap plan without underwriting, Lipschutz said, unless you live in the four states — Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maine and New York — that require guaranteed Medigap issue rights.

The notice you receive should spell out if you get that Medigap purchase right.

Using the nuclear option

What happens if you don't qualify for a Medigap purchase right, but the remaining MA plans don't cover your specific doctors, hospitals or treatments — especially if you are sick? You might want to consider going nuclear.

That means moving completely out of your Medicare Advantage insurer's network — oftentimes to another state, Caughill said. The move allows you to get a guaranteed right to get a Medigap policy without underwriting.

"That's why we call it the nuclear option," she said, "because you have to move."

Caughhill helped four clients this year execute this strategy after the Mayo Clinic, which provides many cancer treatments, stopped taking Medicare Advantage plans.

"For some people it's a matter of life and death," she said.

Where to get help

If your current plan is eliminated or merged, the task of finding a new plan may feel insurmountable, especially given the number of options to compare.

There are places that can help beyond the private Medicare consultants. Lipschutz recommends that seniors contact their state health insurance assistance program, also known as SHIP. You can also reach Medicare's customer support by calling 1-800-MEDICARE.

"Many more people use agents and brokers, some of whom are aboveboard," Lipschutz said. "But some are chasing commissions and steer people towards products that are best for the agent rather than the beneficiary."

data.title: Trump faults aides as Republican midterm prospects dim
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump's blame focuses on Blair as others turn on Wiles
  • President questions campaign spending, redistricting push
  • White House calls criticism 'baseless speculation'

By Nandita Bose, Bo Erickson and Steve Holland

President Donald Trump is blaming senior aides and political operatives for a faltering midterm strategy, questioning campaign spending, faulting redistricting and second-guessing candidate choices as Republicans fight to retain control of Congress, said three people familiar with internal discussions.

Trump is not on the November 3 ballot but repeatedly tells supporters to pretend that he is, hoping to mobilize voters who might otherwise skip the election. He has embarked on a frenetic campaign schedule while largely avoiding acknowledging his own role in shaping the strategy and how his unpopularity is weighing on Republican candidates in competitive races.

Much of the friction has centered on James Blair, the longtime aide who runs Trump's super PAC MAGA Inc., and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, who until now had largely escaped criticism. Trump has faulted Blair's handling of campaign funds, while some White House officials and allies have questioned Wiles' oversight of the political operation.

As Trump questions why campaign spending has failed to improve Republican polling numbers, his advisers are also blaming one another. Wiles has pointed to Blair, while Blair has faulted the White House legislative affairs team, one of the people said.

"What's really happening is a circular firing squad," the person said.

Opinion polls suggest Democrats will win the House of Representatives, while the Senate remains too close to call. Losing the House would hamper Trump's legislative agenda in the final two years of his term and give Democrats subpoena power to investigate his administration.

Trump defended Wiles on Friday, calling her "smart" and "tough" and saying she would remain in her job. "Susie is here, and she's going to be here for a long time," he said.

White House spokesman Davis Ingle rejected the sources' characterization, saying they were "armchair experts peddling their baseless speculation." Wiles did not respond to a request for comment.

TRUMP HAS LONG DISTANCED HIMSELF FROM POLITICAL SETBACKS

Trump has long sought to distance himself from political setbacks. He refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 election and said ahead of the 2022 midterm results that he deserved "all the credit" if Republicans won but "should not be blamed at all" if they lost. More recently, he has reminded audiences that the president's party typically struggles in midterm elections.

But Trump helped devise and drive some of the strategies he is now questioning, including the redistricting effort and candidate choices shaped by his personal loyalties or grievances. His approval rating is at the lowest point of his presidency, weighed down by voter concern over high prices and dissatisfaction with the Iran war.

Trump's frustrations with his political team spilled into public view after Blair and Chris LaCivita, who co-managed Trump's 2024 campaign, traveled in early October to Republika Srpska, a self-governing region of Bosnia. The New York Times reported the men received substantial payments to advise the regional government ahead of local elections.

Trump distanced himself from both men, describing them as "outside consultants" in an October 7 Truth Social post and warning that if he found a conflict of interest, he would "terminate them, immediately!"

Senior White House officials questioned why Blair was taking on lucrative work overseas when he was supposed to be overseeing the final stretch of the Republican campaign, three people said.

One person said Wiles approved the trip without informing Trump, raising questions about how closely she was overseeing his political advisers.

For Trump, the larger concern is that Blair's outside work has distracted him from his political responsibilities, two people said.

In a statement, Blair said: "All of this mudslinging is ridiculous, and counterproductive. President Trump and me are focused on helping Republicans win in November. Every other Republican should be doing the same."

In a separate statement, LaCivita said: "President Trump and his team are and always have been focused on the midterms. That's demonstrated through the money, message and motivation that the president is bringing on the road and all year. Sniping from unnamed cowards who've never been in a fight is not worth responding to."

$200 MILLION AND REDISTRICTING

With Trump asking why Republican polling in pivotal races has not improved despite MAGA Inc.'s campaign spending, which public records put at $200 million so far, it remains unclear whether he will approve more spending before the election, one of the sources said.

Trump also has pressed political aides and advisers in the past week to explain why the redistricting effort he personally pushed has failed to deliver more clear-cut Republican gains, two sources said.

Texas is a particular concern. Republicans redrew the state's congressional map to gain seats, but the strategy relies in part on Hispanic voters turning out as they did for the 2024 election. Opinion polls suggest that support may be difficult to replicate amid concerns about the cost of living and Trump's handling of the economy. Some Republicans fear the new boundaries could backfire, leaving incumbents more vulnerable instead of giving the party an advantage.

"The redistricting diced up the Trump voters too much," one of the sources said.

Trump had said Blair was expected to return to the White House after the midterms, describing his departure as a "short leave of absence." But two sources said his return was now unlikely. "He's not coming back. That is not happening," one of them said.

It was less clear how things would play out for Wiles, who played a central role in Trump's 2024 victory and has been credited by Trump allies and aides with bringing greater discipline to his White House in his second term.

Trump "may be annoyed at certain things but she has effectively kept that machine going," a fourth source close to the White House said.

data.title: Exotic species appear off California thanks to an unusually strong El Niño
data.description:
Key points:
  • Exotic tropical species migrating further north because of El Niño
  • Weather phenomenon followed extended marine heat wave
  • Fishermen love it, but kelp beds harmed and ecosystem altered

By Daniel Trotta and Matt Silverstein

The longfin bigeye fish was spotted in California for the first time last month, and the first sea turtles of any kind nested on California beaches. Meanwhile, a venomous yellow-bellied sea snake swam ashore as whale sharks and hammerheads cruised just off the coast.

Exotic species have been visiting California's shores since an unusually strong El Niño weather phenomenon arrived this year. Occurring naturally every few years, El Niño brings warm ocean water farther north, and tropical species with it, providing California with a stunning visual display that has become ever more evident with the advent of drone and video technology.

"There's kind of a buzz. Fishermen are loving it for sure. I'm as interested as anybody else. It's strange times," said Nate Jaros, vice president of animal care at the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach.

Other visitors include flying fish and manta rays.

California had already experienced an unusual marine heat wave just before its arrival. This year's phenomenon coincided with a string of hurricanes in the eastern Pacific, fueling sea level rise and large waves that have destroyed homes and denuded some Southern California beaches of sand. Preparing for more effects to come this winter, California has declared a state of emergency.

But it has provided a bounty for businesses like Dana Wharf Sportfishing & Whale Watching. Co-owner Donna Kalez said anglers have pulled in 5,000 yellowfin tuna this year, compared to 2 a year ago. They are also landing wahoo and dorado, also known as mahi-mahi, a green fish with a blunt head giving it the profile of a bulldozer.

"Dorado is very exciting because they're very acrobatic, so they jump out of the water. We catch them off kelp paddies, and it's a thrill," Kalez said.

Experts expect conditions to mostly return to normal after El Niño, a natural phenomenon predating human-caused climate change, passes next year. The greatest short-term harm may be to kelp, which thrives in colder waters and provides habitat for multiple species, experts say.

"It’s good for some sharks and probably bad for others," said Chris Lowe, director of the Shark Lab at California State University, Long Beach. "For animals that can't move, that's a bigger problem, right? Most sharks that are highly mobile. They can simply move."

The yellow-bellied sea snake may have venomous fangs but cannot swim like a large shark. When an apparently sick one swam ashore in Orange County in September, a beachgoer used a palm frond to lift it off the sand and drop it in the sea. Jaros said that based on cellphone video he had little doubt it was the yellow-bellied sea snake, Hydrophis platurus.

There have only been six or seven confirmed sightings in California, said William Ludt, associate curator of ichthyology at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County. The last confirmed sighting came during the El Niño of 2015-2016, he said.

Exotic sharks such as the whale shark — a gentle giant and the largest fish on Earth — and the more menacing-looking hammerheads venture into California waters during El Niño. Both have been spotted recently. Lowe said a white shark nursery reappeared for the first time since 2011 in Santa Monica Bay, where juveniles frolic without bothering humans.

Ludt said the aptly named longfin bigeye fish species was recorded for the first time in California this year when an angler caught one on the Venice Fishing Pier in Los Angeles. When two olive ridley sea turtle nests were found on a pair of Orange County beaches in September, they marked the first-ever recorded nest for any sea turtle species on the US West Coast, according to the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The first was discovered by a beachgoer in Seal Beach on September 16, the second by lifeguards in neighboring Huntington Beach three days later, officials said.

And other new species may yet arrive.

"We still aren't fully through it," Ludt said. "It's still very much ongoing."

data.title: ‘AI Can Help India Cut Power Peaks Without Building More Capacity’
data.description:
Smart-meter analytics, behavioural demand response, battery storage and flexible electricity consumption could help distribution utilities manage rising demand while improving renewable energy integration

India’s power distribution utilities could use artificial intelligence (AI), smart-meter data and consumer-led demand response to reduce peak electricity demand and ease pressure on existing grid infrastructure, experts said at the Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) 53rd Foundation Day event in New Delhi on 15 October, 2026.

The approach could help utilities manage rising cooling loads during extreme heat, integrate more renewable energy and defer the need for additional capacity by shifting flexible electricity consumption away from peak hours. Demand response involves encouraging or enabling consumers to adjust when and how they use electricity in response to grid requirements.

As renewable energy generation expands, AI-based forecasting and better use of consumption data could help utilities align electricity demand with periods of higher solar generation while managing evening peaks. India has already established a foundation for demand-side management. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has documented initiatives undertaken by distribution companies, with an estimated potential to reduce demand by around 13,000 MW and save 28 billion units of electricity annually, according to figures presented at the CEA event.

Consumer Behaviour And Storage Can Ease Peak Demand

The experience of Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited (Tata Power-DDL) illustrates how consumer participation can influence peak demand. The utility began experimenting with automated demand response in 2014, initially targeting industrial consumers. Early trials achieved around 7 MW of peak-load reduction across seven to eight events, but concerns about operational control and the limited effectiveness of financial incentives constrained participation. The utility subsequently shifted towards behavioural demand response, allowing consumers to control their electricity use while receiving alerts about anticipated peak periods.

Dwijadas Basak, Chief Executive Officer of Tata Power-DDL, said the programme had expanded to approximately 2.2 lakh consumers. He reported around 500 MW of cumulative load reduction across 17 events conducted during May, June and July. “The motivation that the customers are getting is the sustainability, the pride that they are doing something for the nation, for the environment, for the world,” Basak said, highlighting the role of awareness and recognition in encouraging participation. The experience suggests that demand response cannot depend exclusively on financial incentives. Regular communication, timely alerts and an understanding of consumer behaviour are also necessary to sustain participation.

Abhishek Ranjan, Chief Executive Officer of BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL), highlighted the challenges of managing residential cooling demand during Delhi’s hottest periods, when consumers may be unwilling or unable to reduce air-conditioning use. Battery storage at distribution transformer and grid-substation levels could help address these constraints by supplying electricity during short periods of high demand. Rooftop solar, scheduled electric-vehicle charging and energy-efficient appliances could provide additional flexibility. Ranjan also highlighted the importance of having reliable control over demand-response resources when managing real-time network conditions.

AI Forecasting And Standardisation Can Enable Scale

AI could strengthen demand-response programmes by helping utilities analyse smart-meter readings, weather conditions and consumption patterns to forecast demand more accurately. Appliance-level analysis could help identify flexible loads across residential, commercial and industrial consumers, allowing utilities to estimate how much demand can realistically be shifted during peak periods. Dr Mahesh Patankar, Founder and Managing Director of MP Ensystems Advisory, highlighted the potential to turn smart-meter infrastructure into a continuous source of information for electricity planning.

By combining historical consumption data with weather forecasts and appliance-level insights, utilities could improve predictions of daily, weekly and seasonal demand. Such analysis could also help identify where interventions would deliver the greatest benefits. However, forecasting alone will not resolve every grid constraint. Distribution companies also need common systems to measure outcomes and replicate successful programmes across regions. Prince Dhawan, IAS, Executive Director of REC Limited, identified standardised digital infrastructure as a way to address this challenge.

“If you have to build everything every time from scratch, then nothing will ever scale up,” Dhawan said. For India, the next step is to move from isolated demonstrations towards demand-response programmes that deliver measurable and repeatable results. AI can help utilities anticipate peaks, but meaningful reductions will depend on identifying flexible loads, engaging consumers and establishing systems that allow demand response to operate reliably at scale. As renewable generation increases and electricity consumption patterns evolve, managing when power is used could become as important as expanding how much electricity the country can generate.

Sonali Chawhan

BW Reporters

The author is a Trainee Correspondent at BW Businessworld.

Shareholders also approved amendments to Iveco’s Articles of Association (AoA), its conversion from a publicly listed company into a private limited liability company following delisting, and the appointment of new board members, effective upon settlement.

The resolutions provide for a post-offer demerger, which the acquirer may implement if it secures at least 80 per cent of Iveco’s common shares. Shareholders also authorised a subsequent share sale and the potential dissolution of the existing corporate entity as part of the post-acquisition restructuring.

The EGM further approved changes to Iveco’s special voting share arrangements, including the termination of its loyalty voting structure following settlement.

data.title: Snabbit Posts Rs 168 Cr Loss In FY26 As Quick Home Services Competition Intensifies
data.description:
Snabbit reported a net loss of Rs 168 crore in FY26 on operating revenue of Rs 12.25 crore, as the two-year-old on-demand home services startup invested in customer acquisition, workforce expansion and service delivery amid intensifying competition in the quick home services market, as per a media report.

The company’s operating revenue increased from Rs 26 lakh in FY25 to Rs 12.25 crore in FY26, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). However, its total expenses rose sharply to Rs 195 crore from Rs 6.8 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Founded in 2024 by Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit connects households with trained professionals for tasks such as cleaning, dishwashing and laundry. Customers can book services by the hour, with the platform offering fulfilment within 10 minutes.

Platform services generated Rs 10.82 crore, accounting for 88 per cent of operating revenue in FY26. The remaining revenue came from uniform sales. The company also reported Rs 14.76 crore in other income, primarily from interest earned on bank deposits.

Snabbit’s expenditure included Rs 46 crore in employee benefit costs and Rs 63 crore in expert service costs. It spent another Rs 49 crore on marketing and Rs 23.8 crore on service fulfilment. Banking charges, commissions, recruitment, legal expenses, software maintenance and other overheads contributed to total expenses of Rs 195 crore.

The company’s net loss widened from Rs 5.7 crore in FY25 to Rs 168 crore in FY26. At the unit level, Snabbit spent Rs 15.92 to generate every rupee of operating revenue.

Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -58.45 per cent, while its EBITDA margin was -1,481.63 per cent in FY26.

Snabbit has raised more than USD 112 million to date. Its funding includes a USD 56 million Series D round backed by Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments.

The startup has also reported growth in service volumes. It said it crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day and completed four million home-help jobs during Q1 FY27. Its burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter-on-quarter to below Rs 250.

Agarwal said FY26 was the company’s first full year of operations. During the year, Snabbit expanded from around 500 daily jobs across eight micro-markets to 35,000 daily jobs across more than 100 micro-markets, representing a 75-fold increase in daily jobs. It also acquired nearly one million customers and onboarded more than 20,000 experts.

The founder attributed the Rs 167.8 crore loss to investments in expansion, customer and expert acquisition, and long-term capabilities. He said FY26 financials do not reflect current economics, pointing to improvements in operating leverage and unit economics as the business built greater density across neighbourhoods.

Snabbit is competing with Urban Company’s InstaHelp and Pronto, as companies seek to build demand for on-demand household services. Urban Company’s InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July 2026, ahead of Snabbit’s 1.85 million, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.

Urban Company has also been investing in its quick home services business and has reportedly been looking to raise USD 200 million, as competition in the segment intensifies.

The companies are expanding their customer bases, building workforces and increasing fulfilment capacity. However, their ability to translate higher order volumes into sustainable earnings will depend on worker utilisation, customer acquisition costs, repeat bookings and the density of demand within individual neighbourhoods.

For Snabbit and its competitors, the challenge is to establish a business model in which bookings generate sufficient revenue to cover service delivery and operating costs. Until then, continued expansion may require further funding as the companies work towards improving unit economics.
