Fitness and lifestyle platform Cult.fit has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO), as per a media report. The company plans to raise Rs 950 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 17.86 crore shares by existing shareholders.

The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to repay borrowings, establish new Cult Elite and Cult Neo fitness centres, expand Cultsport exclusive brand outlets, meet lease and rental payments for existing centres, and fund brand marketing and general corporate purposes.

According to the company's draft papers, Cult.fit operated 708 fitness centres across 77 cities in India as of March 31, 2026. Its fitness services business had nearly 9.87 lakh paid members in FY26, while its fitness products business shipped more than 42.3 lakh products during the year.

Cult.fit Revenue Rises 36% In FY26

Cult.fit operates across two main segments: fitness services and fitness products. Fitness services contributed around 70 per cent of its revenue, while fitness products accounted for the remaining 30 per cent.

The company's operating revenue increased 36.26 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,720.61 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,262.93 crore in FY25. It had reported operating revenue of Rs 926.66 crore in FY24.

Its adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.41 per cent in FY26 from -2.76 per cent in FY25, according to the draft papers.

The company operates different fitness centre formats, including Cult Elite, which combines gym workouts with instructor-led group classes, and Cult Neo, which focuses on equipment-based workouts. Its Cultsport brand sells fitness apparel, footwear, equipment and accessories.

Cult.fit also uses a technology-led platform to connect its fitness services and products businesses through its app, website and offline channels.

India’s Fitness Market Projected To Expand

The proposed IPO comes amid growth in India's organised fitness market. According to the Redseer report cited in the draft papers, the country's fitness services market was estimated at Rs 25,600 crore in CY25 and is projected to reach Rs 48,700 crore to Rs 53,100 crore by CY30.

The company's equity shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.

Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs India Securities, Jefferies India, JM Financial and Morgan Stanley India are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

data.title: HDFC Bank reports 5% increase in Q2FY27 standalone net profit at ₹19,510 crore
data.description:
HDFC Bank reported a 5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase in second quarter (Q2FY27) standalone net profit at ₹19,510 crore amid a 10 per cent growth in net interest income and a 4 per cent decline in other income.

India’s largest private sector bank, which is set to see a leadership change with Anup Bagchi, Chief of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance,set to take charge as MD & CEO for three years with effect from October 27, 2026, had logged a net profit of ₹18,641 crore in the year-ago period.

Net interest income (interest income less interest expended) rose 10 per cent y-o-y to ₹34,619 crore (₹31,551.50 crore in Q2FY26).

Other income, including commission income from non-fund based banking activities, fees, earnings from forex and derivative transactions, profit and loss (including revaluation) from investments, dividends from subsidiaries and recoveries from accounts previously written off, declined 4 per cent y-o-y to ₹13,831 crore (₹14,350 crore).

Provisions inched up 2 per cent y-o-y to ₹3,574 crore (₹3,501 crore).

Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) position improved to 1.11 per cent of gross advances as at September-end 2026 against 1.24 per cent as at September-end 2025. Net NPAs position too improved to 0.37 per cent of net advances against 0.42 per cent.

Total deposits grew by a robust 19 per cent y-o-y to stand at ₹33,27,449 crore as at September-end 2026. Advances too rose by a healthy 16 per cent y-o-y to stand at ₹31,95,566 crore as at September-end 2026.

data.title: Festive demand to drive PNB retail loan growth to 17-18%, MSME credit to grow 21%: MD&CEO Ashok Chandra
data.description:
Punjab National Bank (PNB) expects core retail loan growth to reach 17-18 per cent and micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) lending to grow around 21 per cent in the current quarter, with the festive season expected to support credit demand, Ashok Chandra, MD & CEO of Punjab National Bank, told ANI.

The bank also expects agriculture priority-sector lending to maintain its growth momentum after recording 18 per cent growth, as it looks to sustain profitability and improve asset quality in the coming quarters.

“Three areas, retail is doing very well and core retail activity like housing, vacation, mortgage loans, education loan, that is growing at more than 16 percent and I am expecting that this being the festive season, a lot of activities will happen and somewhere around 17 to 18 percent growth should happen in the core retail segment,” Chandra said.

He further added that, “Agriculture priority sector, we are growing at 18 percent and the momentum will continue in this particular quarter also. MSME, we are growing at 20 percent and I'm expecting that in this quarter around 21 percent growth will happen”.

On the bank's overall performance, Chandra said PNB had reported strong growth, asset quality and profitability in every quarter over the past two years and expected the trend to continue. “I'm fully confident that this trend is going to continue in the coming quarters also. You will see the good growth happening across these sectors in the credit. Good growth is happening in the profitability and there will be further reduction in the gross NPA, net NPA,” he said.

PNB sanctioned corporate loans worth ₹2.5 lakh crore in the first two quarters of the current financial year, compared with ₹4 lakh crore during the entire previous financial year.Chandra said the bank was replacing lower-yielding advances with higher-yielding loans, keeping corporate loan-book growth at around 10-11 per cent despite a rise in sanctions.

The strategy helped improve net interest income, with domestic net interest margin (NIM) rising by more than 10 basis points and global NIM by 8 basis points during the quarter. On interest rate, Chandra said the latest 25-basis-point repo rate hike could have a positive impact of around 7 basis points on NIM.

He said lending and deposit rates would be reviewed by the bank's Asset Liability Committee (ALCO) in the coming months, while the RBI would decide on any further rate action based on inflation and growth trends.

data.title: FSSAI initiates legal proceedings against Priyagold Biscuits maker, Dodla Dairy, Ueir Organic Foods
data.description:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSA) has initiated legal proceedings against Surya Food & Agro Ltd, which is known for Priyagold biscuits besides Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd for serious food safety violations. Also, it has issued notices to Narpadham Foods, Sun Ridges Health Carers, and Sha Kantilal Jayantilal.

“The authority maintains zero tolerance for any food safety violations or compromises on public health as per FSS Act 2006, ensuring that strict legal consequences follow for non-compliant food business operators,” the regulator said in a social media post.

In the case of Surya Food & Agro, FSSAI said that an inspection conducted, after receiving a consumer complaint, revealed “serious food safety and hygiene deficiencies.” “Bran meant for cattle feed and not intended for human consumption was being used as a raw material for Priyagold as a source of fiber,” the regulator said in a social media post. Other deficiencies included plant hygiene, pest control, raw material storage and segregation, personnel hygiene, premises maintenance, among others, it added.

“The FSSAI license of Surya Food & Agro has been suspended following serious non-compliances observed during inspection. The competent authority granted sanction for initiating prosecution against Surya Food & Agro for violations,” it noted.

Meanwhile, prosecution has been initiated against Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd after a regulatory sample of Yellow Raisins-an Organic Food was found to be “unsafe due to pesticide residues exceeding prescribed limits,” Upon appeal by the FBO, the sample was sent to a Referral Laboratory, which confirmed that the Yellow Raisin sample was unsafe due to Thiamethoxam and Fluopyram metabolites exceeding the prescribed limit, the food safety regulator said.

Prosecution has also been initiated against Dodla Dairy after a regulatory sample of “Full Cream Milk” was found to be substandard as it did not conform with the milk fat specification prescribed by the regulations. “ Upon appeal by the FBO, the sample was referred to the Referral Food Laboratory, which confirmed that the sample was found to be unsafe due to presence of detergent/ caustic soda and substandard due to the milk fat below the minimum prescribed limits,” the FSSAI said in its post.

FSSAI has sent a notice to Narpadham Foods for various food safety, hygiene and licensing non-compliances. “ The FBO has been asked to review and correct any misleading health or nutrition claims on product labels and promotional materials and remove Retail category from its FSSAI license, as no retail outlet is operated. The FBO must also submit a written explanation, an action taken report and a compliance report within the stipulated time period. Failure to comply may result in suspension or cancellation of the license,” it added.

A notice has been sent to Sha Kantilal Jayantilal, after an inspection found the licensed premises were closed and details have been sought regarding its “actual business activities, the food safety regulator said.

data.title: Death toll in Sept 30 MRPL fire rises to 2
data.description:
The death toll from the September 30 fire at MRPLc’s (Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd) coker hydrotreater unit in phase III rose to two after another contract employee succumbed to injuries on October 17.

One person was killed and 12 injured in the incident on September 30. Of the 12 injured, Rajesh D’Silva, a contract employee, was admitted to hospital with 35 per cent burns on that day. Police said he succumbed to injuries on October 17.

Others with minor injuries had received outpatient treatment on September 30.

The company had earlier said that an incident involving the rupture of a cold separator operating at high pressure in the coker hydrotreater unit resulted in a fire on September 30. The battery limits of the affected unit were immediately isolated to control the situation.

In its notes to the standalone financial results for the second quarter of 2026-27, the company had informed stock exchanges that it has provisionally estimated the financial impact of the September 30 fire incident at ₹118.76 crore.

“Based on a preliminary assessment, the company has provisionally estimated the financial impact of the incident at ₹118.76 crore, comprising the estimated carrying value of the damaged Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), corresponding to an estimated replacement value of approximately ₹225 crore and losses relating to inventories and other incidental expenses,” it said.

The company said the affected assets are adequately insured by it.

data.title: Air India extends temporary suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia until Oct 24 amid Houthi attacks
data.description:
Air India and Air India Express have extended their temporary suspension of flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam in Saudi Arabia until October 24 amid the Houthi rebels’ strikes in the West Asian country. In a travel advisory, Air India said that the bookings issued on or before October 15 with travel dates between October 9 and 25 are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change up to  November 10.

Air India stated, "In view of the prevailing situation, Air India and Air India Express have temporarily suspended flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until 24 October 2026. We understand that these disruptions may affect our guests' travel plans and are committed to providing as much flexibility as possible during this period.”

“Guests holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued on or before 15 October 2026, with travel dates between 9 October and 25 October 2026, are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change on their respective airline up to 10 November 2026. Guests who do not wish to rebook on the originally preferred sector for a future date may, instead, choose to rebook from an alternative station in the GCC region served by their respective airline, subject to availability,” the statement read.

The passengers can also opt for a different destination in West Asia with the airline stating, “Guests choosing the latter option are required to make their own travel arrangements to get to their preferred alternative point of departure and meet the applicable visa and entry requirements. Air India guests may rebook to or from Dubai or Doha. Air India Express guests may rebook to or from Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Bahrain, Doha, Dubai, Kuwait, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Salalah or Sharjah. Guests whose flights have been cancelled may also opt for a full refund if they choose not to travel.”

“We continue to closely monitor the situation and will keep guests informed of any further updates. Our priority remains to support affected guests, minimise inconvenience, and help them continue their journeys with suitable travel options,” Air India said. Several airlines, including IndiGo and Akasa Air, have also temporarily suspended their operations in Saudi Arabia.

The disruptions come after the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with the death toll rising to 13 after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that an Indian national who had been injured in the incident died.

As the conflict escalated, Yemen's internationally recognised government on Friday accused the Houthi militia of targeting Aden International Airport with two missiles that landed near a Yemenia Airlines aircraft preparing for takeoff to Cairo, according to the country's Information Minister Moammar Al-Eryani.

data.title: New steel policy to promote circular economy, boost value addition: Industry
data.description:
The proposed National Steel Policy will promote a circular economy and boost value-added production within India, steel industry stakeholders said.

The policy, which builds a roadmap up to 2027 for the sector, also focuses on decarbonisation of the Indian steel industry, they said.

Pankaj Malhan, MD & CEO of RHI Magnesita India, said the recognition of refractory recovery and magnesite raw material security in the draft policy reflects a holistic approach to build a resilient and competitive steel ecosystem.

"The industry welcomes this policy direction and remains committed to advancing refractory recycling, circular economy initiatives, and investments in India," he said.

BMW Industries Managing Director Harsh Bansal said the policy has taken every aspect of the steel industry into consideration.

It focuses on value-added and coated steel production and lifting of secondary steel players, Bansal said.

Rajib Maitra, Partner, Deloitte India, said the policy envisages reducing the sector's average carbon emission intensity from 2.54 tCO/tcs to approximately 1.54 tCO'/tcs by 2047 through four phases.

Satish Kumar Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Kamdhenu Group, said the emphasis on capacity expansion, raw-material security, technological modernisation, speciality steel and decarbonisation opens significant opportunities for integrated steel producers and secondary steel manufacturers in the country.

Deepak Kumar, Managing Director, PS Raj Steels, said that for downstream manufacturers, support for manufacturing clusters and MSMEs, which account for nearly 60 per cent of flat stainless steel capacity, will matter as much as capacity expansion at the top of the value chain.

The government has released a new steel policy to boost India's crude steel capacity to 604 million tonnes by 2047, enhance industry competitiveness and address key import challenges.

According to the draft National Steel Policy 2047, finished steel demand will rise to 505 MT by 2047, per capita consumption to 302 kg and steel exports to 45 MT.

data.title: Indian state food safety authority names Blinkit, Reliance executives in expired food probe
data.description:
By Arpan Chaturvedi

Indian food safety authorities have named officials of Reliance Group entities and of Eternal’s Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.

The Food and Drug Administration of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai’s most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino’s and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald’s outlet.

The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world’s most populous country.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.

"The disposal agencies ... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.

In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.

Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

INDIA'S INTENSIFYING CRACKDOWN

Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s business group. Zomato’s Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.

The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.

"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."

The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state, three of Reliance and two of Eternal entities, the case documents said.

Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.

In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo , Nestle , Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.

data.title: Bitcoin Is Jordi Visser's ‘Most Asymmetric Bet Ever’ As Tokenization Threatens To Upend Hedge Funds
data.description:
Key points:
  • Jordi Visser called Bitcoin "the most asymmetric bet I've ever made in my life" on Galaxy's podcast on Friday.
  • He said tokenization will push markets toward round-the-clock trading, so prime brokers could remark on hedge fund portfolios on weekends when liquidity is thin.
  • He pointed to Korea's plan for full tokenization by 2027, saying investors would want to trade on Korean prices around the clock to hedge their US portfolios.

Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser called Bitcoin (BTC) "the most asymmetric bet I've ever made in my life," adding that the next big disruption from crypto could land on hedge funds.

Speaking on Galaxy's Galaxy Brains podcast on Friday with Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s (GLXY) Head of Firmwide Research, Visser said his Bitcoin bet was not about the next two or three years, but depended on what he thought would be “happening to all fiat assets relative to something that has no fundamentals.”

Why Tokenization Could Upend Hedge Funds?

Visser, who is a former hedge fund manager, said that hedge funds were already calling him about tokenization. "They're reaching out on what tokenization means," he said, adding that the callers were names most people would recognize.

He explained tokenization meant "the destruction of hedge funds,” because they traded around the clock. In a 24/7 market, prices would keep moving through the weekend. Visser said that meant a hedge fund's entire portfolio could be marked lower on a Sunday, when liquidity was thin, and prime brokers that lend to the fund would notice.

Lenders "know that the price is different and they know that the P&L you're going to have is different," he said. "It puts a much bigger microscope on risk management."

Why Korean Markets Matters

Visser pointed out that the Korean market could force the shift, as it wanted full tokenization by 2027, and its stock market was heavily tied to the memory chip makers at the center of the AI trade.

US hedge funds already checked Korea's KOSPI index first thing in the morning, he said. If Korean stocks traded 24/7, investors would want to hedge their US portfolios at the same time.

"So I challenge anyone who says it isn't going to happen," Visser said. "It might take longer than we all think, but again, we're at zero right now."

Bitcoin Needs A 635% Rally To Reach Visser's Price Target

Previously, Visser has made many bullish calls on Bitcoin. Last month, he said AI-driven demand and tokenization, combined with Bitcoin's scarcity, could push the apex cryptocurrency's price to $600,000 to $1 million if the crypto market expands toward $100 trillion.

Bitcoin's price was trading at $81,612, down by 0.7% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

For Bitcoin to reach the lower band of Visser’s prediction, it would need to rally 635% from its current levels.

data.title: Starlink Says India Infrastructure Ready, Claims Government Approvals In Place Amid Satcom Row
data.description:
Elon Musk-led company says it has worked with Indian regulators for over five years and is ready to offer high-speed internet, as Reliance Industries stresses compliance with Indian laws

Starlink, the satellite internet venture of Elon Musk-led SpaceX, has said it has built dedicated infrastructure in India with the requisite government approvals and is ready to provide high-speed internet services, amid an escalating debate over regulatory clearances and competition in the country's satellite communications market.

In a statement on Friday, the company said it had worked with Indian regulators, industry participants and telecom operators for more than five years to prepare for its entry into the Indian market. The assertion comes as the company awaits the remaining clearances required to begin commercial operations.

The latest development follows a public exchange between Starlink and Reliance Industries over the regulatory framework governing satellite broadband services in India. Reliance has welcomed competition in the sector but maintained that all operators must comply with Indian laws and regulations.

Starlink Highlights Infrastructure Investment

Starlink said its preparations for India included building dedicated ground infrastructure and developing operations to meet the country's regulatory requirements. The company has previously said it established more than 20 gateway sites comprising hundreds of antennas across India.

Lauren Dreyer, Vice-President of Business Operations at SpaceX, had said at the India Mobile Congress that Starlink had developed India-specific security controls and measures to keep Indian user data within the country.

The company has also entered into partnerships with Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio to facilitate its prospective entry into the Indian market, subject to regulatory approvals.

Despite these preparations, Starlink's commercial launch remains contingent on the completion of the outstanding regulatory process, including security-related requirements and foreign direct investment (FDI) approval.

Reliance Emphasises Compliance With Indian Laws

Reliance Industries said on Friday that it did not fear competition from satellite communications providers, including Starlink, but stressed that all companies operating in India must adhere to the country's laws and regulations.

The exchange follows Musk's earlier allegations that unnamed business interests were obstructing Starlink's entry into India to protect their market positions. The government has rejected allegations of discrimination, stating that it follows a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunications services, including satellite communications.

The Ministry of Communications has said security assessments are under way for all three licensed satellite communications operators — Starlink, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance Jio's satellite communications arm. The companies must meet the applicable security requirements before proceeding to the next stage of regulatory approval.

Commercial Launch Awaits Regulatory Clearances

Starlink has secured a Global Mobile Personal Communications by Satellite (GMPCS) licence from the Department of Telecommunications and authorisation from the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe).

However, these approvals alone do not permit the company to commence commercial services. Security clearance, FDI approval and the completion of the spectrum assignment process remain important steps before its launch.

The Department of Telecommunications has backed an administrative allocation framework for satellite spectrum, with a proposed spectrum usage charge of 5 per cent of adjusted gross revenue. The broader framework has also involved government-level approvals and security requirements.

India's satellite broadband market is attracting interest from domestic and international players seeking to provide connectivity in remote and underserved areas. Starlink's eventual entry would add another competitor to the market, where satellite-based services are expected to complement existing terrestrial broadband and mobile networks.
